public_rationale: The numerical claim is strongly corroborated: a snapshot captured at 00:41 UTC on May 25 displays 112 cases, including 19 May decisions versus 15 in April. Assuming 112 at publication and using ChatGPT’s launch as the starting point gives about 0.87 cases per week. Those figures are consistent with Marcus’s qualified comparison. However, the retrieved record does not establish the exact database state when the May 24 post appeared. The combined claim remains unresolved under the publication-time criterion; there is no decisive contradiction.
limitations: The archive timestamp may correspond to May 24 in some time zones, but the post’s publication time and time zone were not established.
Database additions and reporting practices can change documented counts without establishing a change in hallucination probability.
The conditional trend statement is not being treated as an unconditional assertion that May was representative.
